route: Albania has no general independent-means permit for working-age people. Law 79/2021 on Foreigners art. 39 lists the permit grounds. Two fit a non-working couple. Art. 85 'Leje qendrimi per pensionistet' is for foreigners 'qe jane ne pension ne vendin e tyre' (retired), so a 45-year-old couple does not qualify. Art. 84 'Leje qendrimi e perkohshme per perdorim te pasurise se paluajtshme ne pronesi' (temporary permit for owners of Albanian property, up to 1 year, renewable yearly) is the realistic route and is modelled here. VKM 858/2021 lists its documents: title deed, 'Deshmia e burimeve financiare te mjaftueshme' and a personal statement. Proof of means (point 10): an Albanian bank deposit of at least 300,000 ALL per person for a year, or monthly income of at least 32,000 ALL per person. Neither article nor the VKM document list for the property permit names a health-insurance document. Health cover is named for other grounds: the digital-nomad permit ('Police te sigurimit shendetesor, te vlefshme per te pakten 1 vit', which needs work for an employer abroad, so does not fit) and for family reunification, and 'te vertetoje siguracionin shendetesor' for the permanent permit.
policy: FSDKSH voluntary membership of the compulsory scheme (Law 10383/2011). FSDKSH page: 'Per sigurimet shendetesore vullnetare, baza e llogaritjes se kontributit eshte dyfishi i pages minimale', contribution rate 3.4 per cent. The Fund page says that for foreigners the residence-permit number serves as the health-insurance number. Voluntary members have a 6-month waiting period (FSDKSH publication 'Kush Paguan'). Not an income-based charge: the base is fixed at twice the minimum wage.
working: Base per person = 2 x 50,000 ALL = 100,000 ALL a month (50,000 ALL is the monthly minimum wage the Social Insurance Institute (ISSH) page uses for voluntary pension contributions). Contribution = 3.4% x 100,000 = 3,400 ALL a month a person. Couple = 2 x 3,400 = 6,800 ALL a month (81,600 ALL a year).

eu_citizen_difference: An EU/EEA citizen has no health-cover advantage in Albania: no EU rules apply. The Albanian permit rules above do not differ by EU status in the texts read.
spot_check: None reached. Albanian insurers (SIGAL, INTERSIG, SIGMA) publish product terms but quotes only through online forms that need personal details, which the brief forbids. The only price check is internal: 3,400 ALL a person is about 3.4% of 100,000 ALL.
uncertainty: (1) I could not read Law 10383/2011 or the Council of Ministers decision that sets the minimum wage for contributions; the 50,000 ALL figure comes from the ISSH pension page, which is an indirect source. If the health base uses a different minimum wage (the 2025 labour minimum wage was lower), the figure moves in proportion: at 40,000 ALL it would be 2 x 2 x 40,000 x 3.4% = 5,440 ALL for the couple. (2) The Fund's rules on whether a foreigner on a property permit may join voluntarily were not found in a primary text; the Fund's page and the 'Kush Paguan' book say anyone outside the listed groups may join voluntarily and that the permit number serves as the foreigner's insurance number. (3) The property permit lists no health cover, so joining the Fund may be optional in practice. If the couple carried only a private emergency policy, the premium is unknown. (4) Six-month waiting period for voluntary members. Confidence: low to medium.

statutory_must_pay.what: Nothing compulsory. FSDKSH voluntary membership (ALL 6,800 a month for two, the file's `amount`) is optional, so it is left out; see addendum.

private_plan.insurer: Albsig and others (Sigal quotes only on request)
private_plan.product: local private plans, basic to comprehensive
private_plan.terms: Local plans from basic to comprehensive; terms, deductible and waiting periods not stated. Sigal's expat page lists emergency-only options of EUR 5,000-10,000 and gives no prices.
private_plan.pricing: Guide listing Albsig plans from EUR 450 a year (basic) to EUR 610 a year (top tier), and local plans generally EUR 450-760 a year; midpoint of the Albsig range EUR 530 a person a year x 2 / 12 = EUR 88.33 a month. Secondary source, not a tariff; priced in euro as quoted.
